page_subtitles.code_analysis: Reviews source code for quality issues, security vulnerabilities and improvement suggestions using AI. Add a repository, select a file or directory in the tree and start the analysis.
page_subtitles.grafana_analysis: Displays Grafana dashboards inside the app and analyses the shown metrics using AI. Enter the dashboard URL, add it and then start the AI analysis.
page_subtitles.jwt_analysis: Decodes and validates JWT tokens, showing header, payload and signature status at a glance. Paste a token into the text field and click "Analyse".
page_subtitles.review_analysis: Creates AI-powered sprint review reports and exports them as PPTX, Markdown or HTML. Enter the sprint name and sources, then start the analysis.
page_subtitles.ticket_refinement: Prepares a sprint: loads the parent Jira ticket, discovers all linked tickets and asks the AI to produce an improved description and a list of open points for each. The result can be posted as a comment to the respective ticket.
page_subtitles.ticket_creation: Pick the issue type (Story, Technical Task or Bug), describe your requirements in plain text (and optionally attach files) and let AI create a fully structured Sprint ticket that can be directly created in Jira.
page_subtitles.sql_analysis: Analyses SQL queries for syntax errors, performance issues and missing indexes – supports MySQL & MariaDB. Paste the query, optionally add DDL and click "Analyse".
page_subtitles.logging: Paste log output and click "Analyze": all relevant problems (errors, warnings, exceptions, timeouts) are highlighted by color.
page_subtitles.image_extraction: Uses AI to extract text from images (TIFF, PNG, JPG, JPEG). Drop a file, use the in-app file browser, or upload directly – then save the result as a .txt file on the server or download it locally.
page_subtitles.ticket_implementation: Analyses Jira tickets for feasibility, quality and risks – including linked GitLab merge requests. Enter a ticket key and click "Start analysis".
page_subtitles.tooling: Converts any scripts or code snippets into compiled Kotlin tools for StackLens using AI. Paste code, give the tool a name and generate.
page_subtitles.suche: Searches GitLab repositories, databases, Jira and Confluence simultaneously. Enter a search term, select sources and start the search.
page_subtitles.load_test: Analyses PHP code from GitLab for performance bottlenecks – slow DB queries, missing caches, PHP-FPM bottlenecks – and generates a ready-to-run k6 script.
page_subtitles.bug_analysis: Thoroughly analyses repositories for security vulnerabilities and code defects using AI. Add a repository, select it and start the analysis.
page_subtitles.mr_analysis: Reviews GitLab and GitHub merge requests (Code QA) for acceptance criteria fulfillment and adherence to coding guidelines. Enter an MR URL and optionally link a Jira ticket.
page_subtitles.ticket_summary: Loads a Jira ticket and creates a compact AI summary from the description and all comments.
page_subtitles.sprint_review_page: Sprint preparation: enter a Jira sprint name and a target ticket. Every ticket in the sprint is reviewed by the AI and the per-ticket status (✓ Bearbeitet / ? Offene Frage / ✎ Refinement nötig) is appended as an ADF V3 table to the target ticket's description.
page_subtitles.pipeline_analysis: AI-powered analysis of Docker Compose stacks and CI/CD pipelines (GitLab CI, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, …) – detects errors, warnings and smells, suggests optimisations and explains what every key=value means.

load_test.k6_tile_result_info: Shows whether the k6 test succeeded. Green = Exit 0. Red = k6 exited with an error code.
load_test.k6_tile_p95_info: 95th percentile of HTTP response time: 95 % of all requests finished faster than this value. A good indicator of perceived performance under load.
load_test.k6_tile_failrate_info: Percentage of HTTP requests that ended in an error (http_req_failed). Green = 0 %, Yellow = below 5 %, Red = 5 % or more.
load_test.k6_tile_requests_info: Total number of HTTP requests sent (http_reqs). The value below shows the throughput in requests per second.
load_test.k6_tile_duration_info: Total runtime of the k6 test including ramp-up and ramp-down.
load_test.k6_tile_median_info: Median (p50) of HTTP response time: half of all requests finished faster. Less sensitive to outliers than the average.
load_test.k6_tile_p90_info: 90th percentile of HTTP response time: 90 % of all requests finished faster than this value.
load_test.k6_tile_vus_info: Maximum number of concurrently active virtual users (VUs) during the test.
load_test.k6_tile_data_info: Total amount of data received from the server during the test (data_received).
load_test.k6_tile_ttfb_info: Time To First Byte (http_req_waiting): pure server processing time excluding network latency. High values indicate slow backend logic or database queries.
load_test.k6_tile_blocked_info: Wait time for a free TCP slot (http_req_blocked). High values indicate connection pool exhaustion or too many concurrent VUs.
load_test.k6_tile_iters_info: Total number of completed VU iterations (iterations). The value below shows throughput in iterations per second.
load_test.k6_tile_datasent_info: Total amount of data sent to the server during the test (data_sent). Relevant for POST or upload scenarios.
load_test.k6_tile_dropped_info: Number of VU iterations k6 could not start (dropped_iterations). Occurs when VUs are not ready in time — indicates resource exhaustion or an overly aggressive load stage.
load_test.k6_tile_connecting_info: Average time for TCP connection establishment (http_req_connecting). High values indicate network latency or missing keep-alive connections.
load_test.k6_tile_tls_info: Average TLS handshake time (http_req_tls_handshaking). Only appears for HTTPS endpoints. High values indicate expensive certificate verification or missing session reuse.
load_test.k6_tile_stddev_info: Standard deviation of HTTP response time (http_req_duration stddev). High values mean inconsistent response times — the server behaves unevenly under load.
load_test.param_peak_vus_info: Maximum number of concurrently active virtual users at the peak of the load.
load_test.param_ramp_up_info: Time in seconds to gradually increase the number of users from 0 to peak VUs.
load_test.param_steady_info: Time in seconds to hold the load constant at peak VUs – the actual load phase.
load_test.param_ramp_down_info: Time in seconds to gradually reduce the number of users back to 0 after the load phase.

how.title: How does the RAG integration work?
how.l1: On creation or upload, contents are split into chunks, embedded (vectorised) and stored locally — chunk text and metadata in H2, Lucene full-text index and embedding vectors (KnnFloatVectorField) in the Lucene index.
how.l2: The global KI chat searches the local Lucene index with BM25 (full-text search). The user question is never sent to an embedding provider — embeddings are only computed when content is added. Optionally, the query can be rewritten via the KI provider (Query Rewriting) and the top hits re-ranked.
how.l3: Matched sources are surfaced in the chat as citations (e.g. [KB:document-4711#chunk-3]) and as source chips.
how.l4: The embedding configuration is independent from the regular KI configuration. OpenAI, OpenRouter and Ollama are supported.
how.l5: In the Maintenance and Reset tab, “Reset knowledge database” wipes all sources, documents, chunks, vectors and the Lucene index. The factory reset under Configuration → Reset leaves the knowledge base untouched by default; it is also cleared there only when KNOWLEDGE_RESET_ON_FACTORY_RESET=true is set.

add.jira_sprint_hint: Every top-level ticket in the sprint is imported (technical task, bug, support, story, etc.). Subtasks of those tickets are included when "Include sub-tickets" is enabled.
